cohort: The study included 20,535 women who delivered in 10 hospitals in Da Nang, Vietnam, between April 2015 and March 2016.
finding: The study found an overall Caesarean section rate of 58.6% in Da Nang, Vietnam, with higher rates in private hospitals (70.6%) compared to public hospitals (57.9%).
mod_finding: Factors increasing the likelihood of Caesarean sections included the mother being over 30, having an office job, a history of abortions, having a male infant, and a higher neonatal birth weight, as well as previous Caesarean sections, cephalopelvic disproportion, and foetal distress.
birth_weight: Neonatal birth weight was measured as a factor associated with Caesarean section rates.
